Work counters of the last call

Source: R/trace.R
rcs_trace.Rd

With options(rcs.trace = TRUE) the package records the work done by each call of one of its functions: backend calls, catalog files read, data files opened, row groups, candidate and returned rows, and bytes transferred. rcs_trace() returns the records of the last call; rcs_trace_reset() clears them. Counting is deterministic and costs nothing when the option is off.

Usage

rcs_trace()

rcs_trace_reset()

Value

rcs_trace() returns a tibble with one row per counter, detail and location:

  • call: the function that was called, NA for work done outside one;

  • counter: backend_call, catalog_read, file_open, row_groups_total, row_groups_overlap, rows_candidate, rows_returned, bytes_up or bytes_down;

  • detail: the backend operation, the catalog file or the data file;

  • location: the address of the location, NA when there is none;

  • n: the count.

It has zero rows when nothing was recorded. rcs_trace_reset() returns NULL, invisibly.

Examples

withr::with_options(list(rcs.trace = TRUE), {
  rcs_trace_reset()
  rcs_trace()
})
#> # A tibble: 0 × 5
#> # ℹ 5 variables: call <chr>, counter <chr>, detail <chr>, location <chr>,
#> #   n <dbl>
